value.title: F186 replaces background QoS with nice-only builds

sections.name: body
sections.value:
F186 supersedes the older background-QoS build instructions. The authoritative ruling is governance commit f078301c4a26e562ef5e87eae3fc273e413fc6cc, handover/prime-preferences.md, dated 2026-11-11: pij cargo builds and tests run nice -n 19 only, serialized through shared-build's lock, with the four-job default. Do not revive plan 208's taskpolicy requirement or plan 209/F63's automatic --no-run compile/run split from historical plans or old reviewer notes.

#228 b0259b1987d3f829e5494cefa9e366d07404544b applies that ruling to shared-build and route-inventory's separate wrapper. Every supplied cargo command runs once; explicit caller arguments/overrides remain intact. Lock, floor, cap, incremental-off, source touching, stale-lock refusal and process-group draining remain. CI run 42929038558 passed all 19 shared-build fixture cases on both Node 22 and 24. The scheduling fixture proves nice 19 for build/test/doctest even with a fake taskpolicy available; no reviewer-local real cargo build was needed.

When checking removal of an obsolete mechanism, distinguish executable uses from negative tests and historical explanations. A raw grep still finds taskpolicy in AGENTS.md's prohibition, the regression that ensures it cannot run, and history. These are not surviving wrappers. The useful future sensor would reject executable wrapper use, not the mere word.
